analysis.title: FOMC Ahead / RBNZ's Surprise Hold / UK Budget Day / SK Hynix
key_insights: FOMC decision Wednesday: a hold is expected (~90% priced at the 3.75-4.00% range). The uncertainty is Chair Warsh's messaging on insufficient inflation progress, how conditional further tightening sounds, and how much weight he gives financial conditions and uneven growth.

UBS US Economist Jonathan Pingle expects a hawkish hold, with Warsh stressing that inflation is elevated and the job is not done. Rate hikes in December and January remain the base case. Markets price ~80% odds of a 25bp December hike.
Rates may be sensitive to a hawkish surprise because the recent bond rally was driven partly by risk-off flows. US yields have retraced 20-25bp over the past month.

FOMC and hyperscaler earnings (Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon) together test whether the tentative improvement in equity sentiment can become a durable rally. Strong cloud growth and cash generation, easing rates volatility and less hawkish Fed communication would support it. Weaker AI signals or renewed rates pressure would undermine it.

RBNZ held at 2.75% against expectations for a 25bp hike, with a 4-3 vote. NZDUSD fell 1.5%. UBS NZ economist expects 25bp hikes in December and February to a 3.25% terminal rate, well below the 89bp of cumulative hikes OIS prices for June 2027. The desk favours buying AUDNZD dips around 1.2475/85.
Australian Q3 trimmed mean CPI was 1.0% q/q and 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected. Headline CPI was 4.3% y/y vs 4.2% expected. UBS expects a 25bp RBA hike in November, and OIS pricing rose to 22bp from 16bp.

UK Budget (Chancellor Healey's first): expected to favour modest household relief over a fiscal reset. Reuters reports headroom against the tougher fiscal target likely shrinks to GBP15bn from GBP24bn. An upward revision above GBP25bn to next year's financing needs is expected. A bank levy is expected to fund energy support.
UBS FX Compass cut EURUSD targets to 1.1050 (end-2026), 1.1000 (end-Q1 2027) and 1.07 (end-Q2 2027) on French fiscal risk. EURGBP targets cut to 0.8350 (end-Q4) and 0.8200 (end-Q2 2027).

SK Hynix Q3 results were slightly ahead of consensus. A KRW100trn 2026 shareholder-return programme was the main positive, including at least KRW30trn in dividends and KRW60trn in buybacks and cancellations. The dividend rises to KRW20,000 per share. Shares rose 3.5% at the open.
Taiwan's central bank confirmed it is smoothing TWD moves and blamed recent weakness on foreign equity profit-taking. UBS sees risk skewed toward a stronger TWD.
The WSJ reported the US told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign against Iran after the midterms. Oil rose about 1.4% in Asia.

Israeli exit polls point to coalition deadlock. Netanyahu's bloc falls to 50 seats from 68, the opposition bloc including Arab parties reaches 70 vs a 62 threshold, but forming a government looks very difficult and another election is plausible.

BoC is expected to hike 25bp to 2.5% Wednesday, in line with consensus, with another hike seen in January. Chile held at 4.5% for a seventh meeting. The Bank of Thailand is expected to hold at 1.00%, with THB risk skewed weaker if UST yields rebound.

UBS rates sales: the equity/bond correlation flipped negative on Oct 22 (SPX -1.21%, 10s richer 17bp), restoring Treasurys as a risk-off hedge. Oil beta in yields has faded, and OAT/Bund widening has flushed out carry.

China A-share ETFs took in CNY102bn net last week, the strongest since 2024, signalling national team support. UBS derivatives favours 3m CSI 300 call spreads, citing low implied vol, rising outperformance swap rates and YTD-extreme futures discounts.

US equity desk: gains are positioning- and factor-driven (AI and Momentum, short covering), with negative S&P breadth and equal-weight weakness. The question is whether this is tactical covering or a durable rebuild in AI exposure.
Gold stabilised as reserve managers bought below 4,010. The desk is mildly bearish below 4,080-4,085, sees support at 4,025-4,030, and advises against an aggressive short above 4,085.

EURUSD broke 1.1160 support and saw hedge fund selling below 1.1130. The desk expects it to hold around 1.1100 in Asia, with month-end corporate flows Wednesday. USDKRW rose from 1326 toward 1340 on KOSPI hedging flows, with resistance at 1342-43 then 1350.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix's KRW100trn 2026 shareholder-return programme was a key positive surprise and helped offset concerns over AI spending, HBM pricing and capex. Q3 revenue beat UBS's estimate and operating profit was in line.

sector_views.rationale: Energy was the clearest macro laggard on softer crude Tuesday, per the equity derivatives desk. This is a market observation, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix Q3 reported: slightly ahead of consensus. Revenue beat UBS analyst Nicolas Gaudois's estimate and operating profit was in line. A KRW100trn 2026 shareholder-return programme was announced, comprising at least KRW30trn in cash dividends and KRW60trn in buybacks and cancellations, including the KRW40trn repurchase already completed. The cash dividend rises to KRW20,000 per share.
Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon earnings are upcoming, with the FOMC meeting this week. Cloud growth and cash generation are the focus.
Equity derivatives desk: earnings are driving greater dispersion, with clean beats rewarded and misses punished asymmetrically.
